hypothesis: After the code is written, the runs spend 8-10 extra calls (about 45-55k context each, roughly 400k tokens, around half of a run) hand-seeding a user, discovering that the onboarding modal blocks the UI (the introductionVersion web setting), and debugging the Playwright login and page choice. A `uiseed` helper that does the seeding and Playwright setup in one call, plus a prompt change that points to it, removes most of those calls without dropping the UI verification.
changeSummary: Adds bin/uiseed. One call seeds a confirmed and approved user, dismisses the onboarding modal through the Web::Setting record, creates an OAuth token and a public status, and prints TOKEN/SID/AID. It also writes /tmp/pwlib.js with login(), api() and BASE helpers. The Verification bullet in system-prompt.md is rewritten to say to use uiseed, write one combined Playwright script, use /web/statuses/<SID> and /web/accounts/<AID>, and allow at most one harness retry. Everything else in the prompt and config is unchanged.
evidence: Run 2304e9 (792k, 20 calls): calls 11-18 were all UI-harness debugging. #11 seeded the user and wrote the Playwright script. #12 and #13 hit "Welcome to the fediverse" because the onboarding modal was still up. The agent first set user.settings, which was the wrong place. #14-#16 grepped for introductionVersion and Web::Setting. #17 set a huge introductionVersion. #18 swapped /web/public/local for /web/accounts/2 because the public timeline never showed the button. These 8 calls ran at 45-49k context each, so about 380k of the 793k total. Run 0e8a32 (1.08M, 25 calls) shows the same tail: calls 11-25 each carry 47-56k of context and are mostly harness fiddling. Run 4674ce (897k, 23 calls) has a similar tail of calls 11-22. Cache reads are 92% of tokens, so removing whole calls is the lever.
expectedSavings: Target: cut the UI tail from about 8-12 calls to about 3. That is the uiseed call, one Playwright script, and possibly one retry. It saves about 5-8 calls × 48-52k ≈ 250-400k per run. The median should fall from about 880k to roughly 600-700k. Risks: (1) I could not smoke-test uiseed here because Postgres cannot start in the research sandbox (/data is not writable), so the Ruby seed is written from the agent's own working calls in run 2304e9 (User.create!, Web::Setting, Doorkeeper token) and is unverified. (2) A single failed seed would cost a call or two, and the prompt already tells the agent to fall back to the diff review plus the API check. (3) The script only writes DB rows under /tmp-backed services and /tmp files, never app source.
